title: Audit Amancio et al.’s interchangeability and word-network comparisons
statement: Amancio et al.’s reported excess intermittency against global token shuffles is reproduced qualitatively in two public practice editions. All 24 independent page-conditional token streams per layout also exceed that null for both intermittency summaries. Preserving each page’s vocabulary and frequencies reduces the Voynich ratios to 1.005–1.016 and removes significance in both editions. Repeated distinct ordered pairs and reduced directed degree remain after line shuffles and after excluding cross-line adjacency. Pinned self-citation and a stationary one-table reuse chain also depart from the line-preserving null on these metrics, with different effect sizes. The result limits the evidential scope of global shuffles and identifies a residual local order signal for comparisons between specified generators.
check: To repeat the audit, implement the circular recurrence interval exactly and count adjacent identical types and repeated ordered pairs separately. Predeclare the transliteration, line inclusion, seam handling, metrics, and structured controls, then test whole-token, within-page and within-line permutations. Evaluate the metrics jointly against independent realizations and natural texts before making any claim about the source of the local order signal.

evidence.publication_scope: Table 3 reports observed/shuffled mean ratios 1.433 (I), 1.890 (I*), 2.637 (B), and 0.949 (k). Its C* interval 0.981–1.017 is the only displayed one that includes 1. The prose on p. 5 says the other intervals include it, whereas Table 3 and the argument require exclude. The authors report B and I* as exceptions to the comparisons with their natural-language distribution in Table 4. They explicitly propose topic shifts as one reason for increased I*. The authors used ten global shuffles and Eq. 8 error bands. This audit uses permutation tails. Hence its P values cannot be compared numerically to their standardized distances. The article makes no deterministic glyph or language assignment that can be entered as a key.
evidence.input: The public practice Zandbergen–Landini and independent Takahashi transcriptions were intersected on 615 paragraph-line IDs with all tokens certain and in the fixed ordinary EVA letters acdefghiklmnopqrsty. The sample occupies 31 public practice pages. The page and line order of the retained primary lines was kept. Natural controls are contiguous windows with the same token count, sampled using Random(901) from the named pinned works and cut to identical line lengths. These are length-matched illustrations, without a genre or writing-system match. The article’s full manuscript and original corpora are distinct from this layout.

metric_details.I: Mean over word types of frequency at least 5 of population SD of the circular recurrence gaps divided by their mean. Eq. 6 closes the boundary gap so each type’s gaps sum to the stream duration.
metric_details.I50: As for I over the top 50 by count, lexically breaking frequency ties.
metric_details.B_types: Distinct types with at least one self-adjacency, the literal definition in the first-order Statistics section on p. 7. Table 1 labels B Betweenness and the compatibility prose says duplicated bigrams.
metric_details.B_pairs: Alternate literal reading of duplicated bigrams, the number of ordered adjacent pairs occurring at least twice regardless of whether the two tokens are the same type.
metric_details.k_out: Mean distinct outgoing neighbors on the directed adjacency graph described in Methods, retaining a self-loop when present. With fixed length and vocabulary, k_out is directly related to total repeated-edge surplus.
metric_details.s: Mean of twice word count divided by the number of distinct neighbors in either direction, as in Methods. For the seam-exclusion check the convention is to use a denominator of one for a type isolated by removing line boundaries.
metric_details.s50: s over the 50 most frequent types.

evidence.method: Primary ratios use observed metric divided by the permutation mean. The longer manuscript run uses 999 permutations at each of the global, page and line levels, independently in both editions, fixed NumPy seed 98900 plus 100 per successive null. Each two-sided P is twice the smaller add-one tail probability clipped at one, counting ties in each tail. Holm adjusted values cover seven metrics within each edition and each null. The adjacency sensitivity excludes between-line edges on every permutation. I and I50 in that check are unchanged because time still runs across the retained token sequence. Simulations and natural controls use 99 permutations, with unadjusted rejection counts provided only as calibration summaries. All input distinctions are fixed across permutations.
evidence.generators: Pinned vs.generators.g_self_citation and g_grille use the public fit pages. Six additional one-table whole-word-reuse backgrounds use the stationary copy condition of P-R-009/P-J-005 fitted on the public fit pages, with no edit reuse or time drift. The stationary iid and piecewise iid controls have 1,536 possible abstract tokens and Zipf weights proportional to rank^-0.9. In the piecewise case six independent probability vectors each blend 70% randomly permuted Zipf weights and 30% original weights and are assigned to six consecutive equal-page-count groups by floor(6i/P) for zero-based page i. The iid token drawings are independent conditional on the probability vector, so they contain no local transition rule. Generator seeds 901–908, stationary-copy seeds 901–906, iid seeds 901–924.
evidence.limitations: Topology measures beyond the explicit degree and selectivity implementations, the approach to language ranking, and the paper’s compatibility density estimates were outside scope. Single windows from four books do not reproduce its language reference distribution. Generated texts illustrate multiple mechanisms behind a rejection. A match to a direction or a null rejection can occur with materially different effect sizes.
